title: Changes in axial length in anisometropic children wearing orthokeratology lenses

notes: Retrospective chart review of 148 children with myopic anisometropia aged 8-14 years at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University (China), January 2017 to September 2019; the authors state that all patients meeting the inclusion criteria were included; the number of children screened or lost is not reported, and every included child is tabulated at baseline and 1 year.
Inclusion required a treatment-zone decentration < 1 mm during orthokeratology wear (a lens-fitting criterion assessed during treatment, not an axial-length outcome).
Subgroups are defined by the baseline SER of the untreated fellow eye (low myopia, emmetropia, low hyperopia), i.e. before treatment.
Eyes are not right/left: each series is one eye per child (the treated more myopic eye or the untreated fellow eye).
Units: millimetres (row labels 'AL ... (mm)'). Device: IOLMaster-500 (Carl Zeiss).

SER, corneal power, corneal astigmatism, central corneal thickness, intraocular pressure and anterior chamber depth are tabulated in Table 1 and not extracted; SER at baseline is also in Table 2 row R4.
